title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二 武帝中
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二 武帝中 Volume 2 Annals 2: Emperor Wu 2

sentences.zh: 七年正月己未，振旅于京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, on the day jiwei, he led the army back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year (411), on the day jiwei, Gaozu marched his troops back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 改授大將軍、揚州牧，給班劍二十人，本官悉如故，固辭。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou, granted twenty ceremonial swords, and all his original offices were left unchanged; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The court offered him Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou, with twenty ceremonial swords and all his old posts unchanged. He refused.

sentences.zh: 凡南北征伐戰亡者，並列上賻贈。

translations.literal: All who had died in battle on the northern and southern campaigns were to be listed and presented for funeral subsidies.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a full list of those killed in the northern and southern campaigns, with funeral grants for each.

sentences.zh: 尸喪未反，遣主帥迎接，致還本土。

translations.literal: Where the dead had not yet been brought back, he sent the commanders to receive them and return them to their native districts.
translations.idiomatic: Where bodies had not yet come home, he sent the field commanders to escort them back to their home districts.

sentences.zh: 二月，盧循至番禺，為孫季高所破，收餘眾南走。

translations.literal: In the second month, Lu Xun reached Panyu, was defeated by Sun Jigao, gathered his remaining forces, and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lu Xun reached Panyu. Sun Jigao defeated him; he gathered what was left of his army and fled south.

sentences.zh: 劉藩、孟懷玉斬徐道覆于始興。

translations.literal: Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: At Shixing, Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu.

sentences.zh: 晉自中興以來，治綱大弛，權門并兼，強弱相凌，百姓流離，不得保其產業。

translations.literal: Since the Jin restoration, the bonds of governance had greatly slackened; powerful houses annexed one another, the strong bullied the weak, and the common people were displaced and could not keep their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin court moved south, government had grown lax. Great families swallowed their neighbors, the strong preyed on the weak, and ordinary people lost their homes and could not hold on to their land.

sentences.zh: 桓玄頗欲釐改，竟不能行。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan had wished somewhat to reform this, but in the end could not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had tried to set things right, but never managed to.

sentences.zh: 公既作輔，大示軌則，豪強肅然，遠近知禁。

translations.literal: Once Gaozu had become regent, he displayed great norms; the powerful were awed into order, and near and far learned what was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozu took power as regent, he laid down clear rules. The mighty fell silent, and everyone, near and far, knew the law.

sentences.zh: 至是會稽餘姚虞亮復藏匿亡命千餘人。

translations.literal: At this time Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji again harbored more than a thousand fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji was again sheltering over a thousand fugitives.

sentences.zh: 公誅亮，免會稽內史司馬休之。

translations.literal: Gaozu executed Liang and dismissed Sima Xiuzhi, Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had Liang executed and removed Sima Xiuzhi as Interior Minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 天子又申前命，公固辭。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again pressed the earlier appointment upon him, and Gaozu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed the earlier honors on him again. Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 於是改授太尉、中書監，乃受命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reassigned as Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and then accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and this time he accepted.

sentences.zh: 奉送黃鉞，解冀州。

translations.literal: The court presented the yellow battle-axe, and he relinquished Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent him the yellow battle-axe; he gave up Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史杜慧度斬盧循，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiaozhou Du Huidu beheaded Lu Xun and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu, Inspector of Jiaozhou, killed Lu Xun and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是諸州郡所遣秀才、孝廉，多非其人，公表天子，申明舊制，依舊策試。

translations.literal: Previously the Recommended Scholars and Filial and Incorrupt candidates sent up by the provinces and commanderies had often not been fit men; Gaozu memorialized the Son of Heaven, clarifying the old regulations and restoring the written examinations as before.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial nominees for office had often been unworthy. Gaozu petitioned the throne to restore the old examination system.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍、荊州刺史道規疾患求歸，八年四月，改授豫州刺史，以後將軍、豫州刺史劉毅代之。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui, ill, asked to return; in the fourth month of the eighth year he was reassigned as Inspector of Yuzhou, and Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou Liu Yi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, fell ill and asked to come home. In the fourth month of the eighth year (412) he was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Yi, Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou, took his place in Jing.

sentences.zh: 毅與公俱舉大義，興復晉室，自謂京城、廣陵，功業足以相抗。

translations.literal: Yi had raised the great cause together with Gaozu and restored the Jin house; he considered that his achievements at the capital and at Guangling were enough to rival Gaozu's.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had joined Gaozu in restoring the Jin dynasty and thought his deeds at the capital and at Guangling matched Gaozu's own.

sentences.zh: 雖權事推公，而心不服也。

translations.literal: Though in power he deferred to Gaozu, in his heart he was not content.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded to Gaozu in public, but in his heart he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 毅既有雄才大志，厚自矜許，朝士素望者多歸之。

translations.literal: Yi possessed great talent and high ambition and thought highly of himself; many courtiers of long-standing repute turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was talented, ambitious, and vain. Many senior officials looked to him instead.

sentences.zh: 與尚書僕射謝混、丹陽尹郗僧施並深相結。

translations.literal: He was deeply allied with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun and Chief of Danyang Xi Sengshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Xie Hun, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Xi Sengshi, Chief of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 及西鎮江陵，豫州舊府，多割以自隨，請僧施為南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When he went west to Jiangling, the old offices of Yuzhou were largely carved up for his own use, and he requested that Sengshi be made Commander Who Pacifies the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held Jiangling in the west, he took over much of the old Yuzhou establishment and asked that Sengshi be made Commander Who Pacifies the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 既知毅不能居下，終為異端，密圖之。

translations.literal: Knowing that Yi could not remain subordinate and would in the end become a rebel, he secretly laid plans against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu saw that Yi would never stay below him and would turn rebel; he began to plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 毅至西，稱疾篤，表求從弟兗州刺史藩以為副貳，偽許焉。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the west he claimed grave illness and memorialized, asking that his younger cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made his deputy; this was falsely granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reached the west, claimed to be gravely ill, and asked that his cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made his deputy. Gaozu pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 九月，藩入朝，公命收藩及謝混，並於獄賜死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, when Fan entered court, Gaozu ordered Fan and Xie Hun seized and both were granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fan came to court. Gaozu had him and Xie Hun arrested and executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 自表討毅。

translations.literal: He himself memorialized to campaign against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to take the field against Yi.

sentences.zh: 又假黃鉞，率諸軍西征。

translations.literal: He was also lent the yellow battle-axe and led the armies west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the yellow battle-axe and marched west at the head of the armies.

sentences.zh: 以前鎮軍將軍司馬休之為平西將軍、荊州刺史，兗州刺史道憐鎮丹徒，豫州刺史諸葛長民監太尉留府事，加太尉司馬、丹陽尹劉穆之建威將軍，配以實力。

translations.literal: Former General Who Guards the Army Sima Xiuzhi was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Inspector of Yanzhou Daoling garrisoned Dantu; Inspector of Yuzhou Zhuge Changmin oversaw the Grand Commandant's headquarters; and Grand Commandant Marshal and Chief of Danyang Liu Muzhi was made General Who Establishes Might, each posted with real force.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Daoling held Dantu; Changmin ran the capital in Gaozu's absence; Muzhi was made General Who Establishes Might—all with real troops behind them.

sentences.zh: 壬午，發自京師。

translations.literal: On the day renwu he set out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu he marched out from the capital.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍王鎮惡、龍驤將軍蒯恩前襲江陵。

translations.literal: He sent Staff Officer Wang Zhen'e and Dragon-Chariot General Kuai En ahead to strike Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Zhen'e and Kuai En ahead to take Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十月，鎮惡剋江陵，毅及黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zhen'e took Jiangling; Yi and his partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhen'e took Jiangling. Yi and his followers were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，公至江陵，下書曰：

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the eleventh month, Gaozu reached Jiangling and issued a proclamation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao in the eleventh month Gaozu reached Jiangling and issued a proclamation:

sentences.zh: 夫去弊拯民，必存簡恕，捨網修綱，雖煩易理。

translations.literal: "To remove abuses and save the people, one must preserve simplicity and forbearance; to cast aside the net and repair the cords, though troublesome, is easy to justify in principle."
translations.idiomatic: "To cure abuses and help the people, government must stay simple and humane. Tightening the law after years of disorder is hard work, but it is the right course."

sentences.zh: 江、荊彫殘，刑政多闕，頃年事故，綏撫未週。

translations.literal: Jiang and Jing were wasted and maimed; penal administration had many gaps; in recent years, because of upheaval, pacification had not been thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Jing were devastated; justice was patchy; years of turmoil had left the region half-settled.

sentences.zh: 遂令百姓疲匱，歲月滋甚，財傷役困，慮不幸生。

translations.literal: Thus the common people grew exhausted and impoverished, month by month the harm deepened, wealth was injured and corvée labor distressed, and I feared misfortune might arise.
translations.idiomatic: The people grew poorer every month, taxes and labor broke them, and I feared worse would follow.

sentences.zh: 凋殘之餘，而不減舊，刻剝徵求，不循政道。

translations.literal: On what remained of the wasted land, levies were not reduced from old levels; exactions and requisitions did not follow the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Even on ruined ground the old levies stood. Officials squeezed the people without regard to law.

sentences.zh: 宰莅之司，或非良榦，未能菲躬儉，[1]苟求盈給，積習生常，漸不知改。

translations.literal: The officials who presided over districts were not always capable men; they could not restrain themselves in frugality, [1] but sought only to fill quotas; accumulated habit became custom, and gradually they no longer knew how to change.
translations.idiomatic: Many local magistrates were unfit. They would not live plainly [1] but chased every quota until waste became habit and reform seemed impossible.

sentences.zh: 近因戎役，來涉二州，踐境親民，愈見其瘼，思欲振其所急，卹其所苦。

translations.literal: Recently, because of the military campaign, I have come to these two provinces; treading the borders and facing the people, I have seen their afflictions all the more clearly, and I wish to rouse what is urgent and relieve what is bitter.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign has brought me into both provinces. Seeing the people myself, I know their distress and mean to ease what hurts them most.

sentences.zh: 凡租稅調役，悉宜以見戶為正。

translations.literal: All rent, tax, and corvée levies should be based entirely on registered households as they stand.
translations.idiomatic: All rent, tax, and labor duties shall be assessed only on actual registered households.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣屯田池塞，諸非軍國所資，利入守宰者，今一切除之。

translations.literal: Garrison fields, ponds, and passes in the provinces, commanderies, and counties—whatever did not serve military or state needs but whose profits went to the guarding magistrates—are now all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial garrison farms, ponds, and toll stations that served private profit rather than the army or the state are abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣吏，皆依尚書定制實戶置。

translations.literal: Officials in the provinces, commanderies, and counties shall all be appointed according to the Masters of Writing's fixed quotas for actual households.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial, commandery, and county staffs shall be set only at the numbers the Masters of Writing allow for real households.

sentences.zh: 臺調癸卯梓材，庚子皮毛，可悉停省，別量所出。

translations.literal: The court requisitions of guimao timber and gengzi hides may all be halted and reduced; other sources shall be measured instead.
translations.idiomatic: Court demands for guimao timber and gengzi hides are suspended; other supplies will be found.

sentences.zh: 巴陵均折度支，依舊兵運。

translations.literal: The Ba-ling equalization and expenditure office shall follow the old military transport rules.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba-ling equalization office shall return to the old military transport system.

sentences.zh: 原五歲刑已下。

translations.literal: Pardon all punishments of five years or less.
translations.idiomatic: All sentences of five years or less are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 凡所質錄賊家餘口，亦悉原放。

translations.literal: All dependents of rebel households held as pledges are likewise to be released.
translations.idiomatic: Dependents taken hostage from rebel families are also freed.

sentences.zh: 以荊州十郡為湘州，公乃進督。

translations.literal: Ten commanderies of Jingzhou were made into Xiangzhou, and Gaozu then advanced as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commanderies of Jing were split off as Xiang province, and Gaozu took overall supervision.

sentences.zh: [2]以西陽太守朱齡石為益州刺史，率眾伐蜀。

translations.literal: [2] Administrator of Xiyang Zhu Lingshi was made Inspector of Yizhou and led the armies to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Zhu Lingshi, Administrator of Xiyang, was made Inspector of Yizhou and marched against Shu.

sentences.zh: 進公太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆鼓吹，班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Gaozu was promoted to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with feathered canopy, drums, and whistles, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with imperial music and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 九年二月乙丑，公至自江陵。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the second month of the ninth year, Gaozu returned from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou in the second month of the ninth year (413) Gaozu returned from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初諸葛長民貪淫驕橫，為士民所患苦，公以其同大義，優容之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhuge Changmin had been greedy, licentious, arrogant, and overbearing, a affliction to scholars and commoners; Gaozu, because he had shared the great cause, treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin had long been greedy, brutal, and hated by the people. Gaozu had tolerated him because they had fought together for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 劉毅既誅，長民謂所親曰：「昔年醢彭越，今年誅韓信，禍其至矣。

translations.literal: After Liu Yi was executed, Changmin said to those close to him: "Last year they minced Peng Yue; this year they kill Han Xin—disaster is upon me.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died, Changmin told his intimates, "Last year Peng Yue was boiled; this year Han Xin is killed. My turn is coming.

sentences.zh: 」將謀作亂。

translations.literal: " He was about to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He began to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 公克期至京邑，而每淹留不進。

translations.literal: Gaozu had set a date to reach the capital, yet each day he delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had named a day to reach the capital, but lingered on the road.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下頻日奉候於新亭，長民亦驟出。

translations.literal: From the Three Dukes down, for days on end they went to wait upon him at Xinting; Changmin too came out repeatedly in haste.
translations.idiomatic: For days the highest officials waited on him at Xinting. Changmin kept hurrying out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 既而公輕舟密至，已還東府矣。

translations.literal: Presently Gaozu came secretly in a light boat and was already back at the eastern headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Then Gaozu slipped in by light boat and was already back at his eastern headquarters.

sentences.zh: 長民到門。

translations.literal: Changmin came to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin came to the gate.

sentences.zh: 引前，卻人閑語，凡平生於長民所不盡者，皆與及之。

translations.literal: Gaozu drew him forward, dismissed the attendants, and in private conversation went over everything in their lives that he had never yet said to Changmin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu brought him in, sent everyone else away, and spoke with him at length about everything he had never yet said between them.

sentences.zh: 長民甚說。

translations.literal: Changmin was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin was delighted.

sentences.zh: 已密命左右壯士丁旿等自幔後出，於坐拉焉。

translations.literal: He had already secretly ordered the strong men at his side, Ding Wu and the rest, to come out from behind the curtain and seize him where he sat.
translations.idiomatic: He had already told his strongmen, Ding Wu and the rest, to slip out from behind the curtain and seize him in his seat.

sentences.zh: 長民墜牀，又於地毆之，死於牀側。

translations.literal: Changmin fell from the couch; they beat him again on the ground, and he died beside the couch.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin fell from the couch. They beat him on the floor until he died beside it.

sentences.zh: 輿尸付廷尉。

translations.literal: His body was placed in a cart and handed over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The body was carted to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 并誅其弟黎民。

translations.literal: His younger brother Limin was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Limin was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 旿驍勇有氣力，時人為之語曰：「勿跋扈，付丁旿。」

translations.literal: Wu was fierce and brave and full of strength; at the time people made a saying of it: "Do not act the bully—hand it to Ding Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Wu was famously fierce. People said, "Don't play the tyrant—leave it to Ding Wu."

sentences.zh: 先是山湖川澤，皆為豪強所專，小民薪採漁釣，皆責稅直，至是禁斷之。

translations.literal: Previously, mountains, lakes, rivers, and marshes had all been monopolized by the powerful; common people gathering firewood, fishing, or cutting reeds all paid a tax; now this was forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families had seized lakes, rivers, and hills; even firewood and fishing carried a fee. That was now forbidden.

sentences.zh: 時民居未一，公表曰：

translations.literal: At the time the people were not yet settled in one place; Gaozu memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The people were still unsettled. Gaozu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞先王制治，九土攸序，分境畫疆，各安其居。

translations.literal: I have heard that the former kings in establishing order arranged the nine domains in sequence, divided borders and drew boundaries, and each kept to his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings ordered the realm by fixing borders so that each people could dwell in peace.

sentences.zh: 在昔盛世，人無遷業，故井田之制，三代以隆。

translations.literal: In past ages of flourishing rule, men did not change their occupations; thus the well-field system flourished through the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In great ages no one left his trade; that is why the well-field system lasted through the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 秦革斯政，漢遂不改，富強兼并，於是為弊。

translations.literal: Qin overturned this policy; Han did not change it, and the strong annexed the rich—thus the abuse arose.
translations.idiomatic: Qin abolished that order; Han kept the change, and the strong swallowed the weak.

sentences.zh: 然九服弗擾，所託成舊，在漢西京，大遷田、景之族，以實關中，即以三輔為鄉閭，不復係之於齊、楚。

translations.literal: Yet the nine domains were not disturbed; what they relied on remained the old. In the Western Han capital, the clans of Tian and Jing were moved on a great scale to fill Guanzhong, and the Three Metropolises became their native hamlets, no longer tied to Qi and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Still the realm held together because people kept their roots. In Western Han the Tian and Jing clans were moved en masse into Guanzhong; the capital districts became home and they were cut off from Qi and Chu.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉播越，爰託淮、海，朝有匡復之算，民懷思本之心，經略之圖，日不暇給。

translations.literal: From the Yongjia turmoil onward, the court entrusted itself to the Huai and the sea; the court had plans to restore the realm, and the people cherished the wish to return to their roots; schemes of strategy left no day free.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongjia the court fled to the Huai and the sea. All wanted restoration, and the people longed for home, but war left no day for civil rule.

sentences.zh: 是以寧民綏治，猶有未遑。

translations.literal: Thus in settling the people and pacifying rule, there was still no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Peaceful settlement had to wait.

sentences.zh: 及至大司馬桓溫，以民無定本，傷治為深，庚戌土斷，以一其業。

translations.literal: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen saw that the people had no fixed base and that harm to governance lay deep therein, in the year gengxu he carried out the land register to unify their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen saw that people had no fixed domicile and government suffered for it, he carried out the gengxu land register in 365 to give everyone a single legal home.

sentences.zh: 于時財阜國豐，實由於此。

translations.literal: At that time wealth flourished and the state was rich—this was truly owing to that measure.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury grew rich because of it.

sentences.zh: 自茲迄今，彌歷年載，畫一之制，漸用頹弛。

translations.literal: From then until now, many years have passed; the unified system has gradually fallen into decay.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the unified system had slowly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 雜居流寓，閭伍弗修，王化所以未純，民瘼所以猶在。

translations.literal: Mixed residence and floating registration, neighborhood registers not kept in order—the royal transformation was therefore not pure, and the people's afflictions therefore remained.
translations.idiomatic: Migrants and false registers broke the wards; government never fully took hold, and the people's misery remained.

sentences.zh: 臣荷重任，恥責實深，自非改調解張，無以濟治。

translations.literal: I bear a heavy commission and am deeply ashamed of the gap between charge and result; unless I change the registers and loosen the bonds, I cannot bring order.
translations.idiomatic: I hold great power and am ashamed that rule still fails. Without fixing the registers I cannot govern.

sentences.zh: 夫人情滯常，難與慮始，所謂父母之邦以為桑梓者，誠以生焉終焉，敬愛所託耳。

translations.literal: Human feeling clings to the constant and finds it hard to plan at the beginning; what is called taking one's native district as one's mulberry tree is truly because one is born and dies there and the object of reverent love is entrusted there.
translations.idiomatic: People cling to habit and hate sudden change. They call their home a mulberry tree because they are born and buried there and their loyalty belongs there.

sentences.zh: 今所居累世，墳壟成行，敬恭之誠，豈不與事而至。

translations.literal: Where they now dwell for generations, graves and mounds stand in rows; the sincerity of reverence—how could it fail to attend upon the matter when it comes?
translations.idiomatic: Families have lived in one place for generations; their graves line the fields. How could they not care when the state asks them to move?

sentences.zh: 請準庚戌土斷之科，庶子本所弘，稍與事著。

translations.literal: I ask that the gengxu land-register statute be applied, so that the intent to honor native roots may be broadly carried out and may gradually show in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the gengxu land register be enforced again, so respect for native roots may guide policy.

sentences.zh: 然後率之以仁義，鼓之以威武，超大江而跨黃河，撫九州而復舊土，則戀本之志，乃速申於當年，[3]在始暫勤，要終所以能易。

translations.literal: Then, leading them with benevolence and righteousness and rousing them with martial might, crossing the great river and spanning the Yellow River, comforting the nine provinces and recovering the old lands—then the wish to cherish one's roots would quickly be fulfilled in that year, [3] a brief hardship at the start, but in the end the change could be made easy.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with benevolence and force together, we may cross the Yangtze and Yellow River, recover the north, and give every man his home again. [3] The pain at first will be brief; in the end the change will be easy.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，垂矜萬民，憐其所失，永懷鴻雁之詩，思隆中興之業。

translations.literal: Bow your head, Your Majesty, pitying the myriad people, cherishing what they have lost, ever keeping in mind the ode of the wild geese, thinking to exalt the enterprise of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pities the people, remembers what they have lost, and keeps the ode of the wild geese in mind, longing to restore the realm.

sentences.zh: 既委臣以國重，期臣以寧濟，若所啟合允，請付外施行。

translations.literal: Having entrusted me with the weight of the state and expecting me to bring peace, if what I propose is fitting, I ask that it be sent out and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: You have charged me with the realm and expect peace from me. If this plan is sound, let it be carried out.

sentences.zh: 於是依界土斷，唯徐、兗、青三州居晉陵者，不在斷例。

translations.literal: Thereupon land was registered according to boundaries; only those in Jinling from Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces were outside the statute.
translations.idiomatic: Land was then registered by district. Only households of Xu, Yan, and Qing living in Jinling were exempt.

sentences.zh: 諸流寓郡縣，多被併省。

translations.literal: Many of the floating commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Many refugee commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.

sentences.zh: 以公領鎮西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 公固讓太傅、州牧及班劍，奉還黃鉞。

translations.literal: Gaozu firmly declined Grand Tutor, Governor of the province, and the ceremonial swords, and returned the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused the Grand Tutorship, the governorship, and the ceremonial swords, and sent back the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 七月，朱齡石平蜀，斬偽蜀王譙縱，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Zhu Lingshi pacified Shu, beheaded the false King of Shu Qiao Zong, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhu Lingshi conquered Shu, killed the pretender Qiao Zong, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，封公次子義真為桂陽縣公，以賞平齊及定盧循也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Gaozu's second son Yizhen was enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyang, to reward the pacification of Qi and the defeat of Lu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Gaozu's second son Yizhen was made Duke of Guiyang, rewarding the conquest of Qi and the defeat of Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 天子重申前命，授公太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆、鼓吹、班劍二十人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again pressed the earlier appointment: Gaozu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with feathered canopy, drums, whistles, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again pressed the old honors on him: Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, imperial music, and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 將吏百餘敦勸，乃受羽葆、鼓吹、班劍，餘固辭。

translations.literal: More than a hundred officers urged him earnestly; only then did he accept the feathered canopy, drums, whistles, and ceremonial swords; the rest he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred officers begged him to accept. He took the music and swords but refused the rest.

sentences.zh: 十年，息民簡役。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he gave the people rest and simplified corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (414) he eased burdens on the people and cut labor duties.

sentences.zh: 築東府，起府舍。

translations.literal: He built the eastern headquarters and raised the official residences.
translations.idiomatic: He built the eastern headquarters and its offices.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍、荊州刺史司馬休之，宗室之重，又得江漢人心，公疑其有異志，而休之兄子譙王文思在京師，招集輕俠，公執文思送還休之，令自為其所。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Sima Xiuzhi was a man of weight in the imperial clan and had won the hearts of the Jiang and Han regions; Gaozu suspected he harbored a different intent. Xiuzhi's elder brother's son, the Marquis of Qiao Wen Si, was in the capital gathering daredevils; Gaozu seized Wen Si and sent him back to Xiuzhi, telling him to deal with the matter himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, was a prince of the blood with a following in Jiang and Han. Gaozu distrusted him. Xiuzhi's nephew Wen Si was in the capital gathering ruffians; Gaozu arrested Wen Si and sent him to Xiuzhi to punish as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 休之表廢文思，并與公書陳謝。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized to dismiss Wen Si and also wrote Gaozu a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi memorialized to disown Wen Si and wrote Gaozu to apologize.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，公收休之子文寶、兄子文祖，並於獄賜死，率眾軍西討。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, Gaozu seized Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his brother's son Wenzu and granted them death in prison, then led the armies west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year (415) Gaozu had Wenbao and Wenzu executed in prison and marched west.

sentences.zh: 復加黃鉞，[4]領荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again given the yellow battle-axe [4] and took charge as Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again given the yellow battle-axe [4] and made Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，發京師，以中軍將軍道憐監留府事。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi he set out from the capital; Central Army General Daoling oversaw the headquarters left behind.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi he left the capital. Daoling ran affairs at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 休之上表自陳曰：

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized in his own person, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi submitted a personal memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞運不常一，治亂代有，陽九既謝，圮終則泰。

translations.literal: I have heard that fortune is not constant, order and disorder succeed each other in turn; when the yang ninth calamity has passed, collapse at the end gives way to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune never stays the same; order and chaos take turns. When the worst is past, ruin gives way to renewal.

sentences.zh: 昔篡臣肆逆，皇綱絕紐，卜世未改，[5]鼎祚再隆。

translations.literal: In former days the usurping minister ran riot, the imperial cords were severed, the allotted age was not yet changed, [5] and the sacred vessel was raised a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Once a usurper seized power and the dynasty seemed dead, yet the throne was restored [5] and the mandate lived again.

sentences.zh: 太尉臣裕威武明斷，道建義旗，除蕩元凶，皇居反正。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was martially awesome and brilliantly decisive; he raised the banner of righteousness, swept away the chief villain, and restored the imperial palace to right order.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was fierce and clear-sighted. He raised the righteous standard, destroyed the usurper, and brought the throne back to order.

sentences.zh: 布衣匹夫，匡復社稷，南剿盧循，北定廣固，千載以來，功無與等。

translations.literal: A commoner in plain cloth restored the altars of state; south he exterminated Lu Xun, north he pacified Guanggu—for a thousand years there has been no equal to his merit.
translations.idiomatic: A man born in humble rank had restored the dynasty: he crushed Lu Xun in the south and conquered Guanggu in the north; in a thousand years no feat could match his.

sentences.zh: 由是四海歸美，朝野推崇。

translations.literal: Thus the four seas turned in praise, and court and countryside exalted him.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven sang his praise; court and country alike held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 既位窮台牧，權傾人主，不能以道處功，恃寵驕溢。

translations.literal: Once he had reached the pinnacle of terrace and pasturage office, his power overbalanced the sovereign; he could not treat his achievements by the Way, and relied on favor to grow arrogant and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen to the highest command, his power eclipsed the throne itself. He no longer knew how to weigh his merit with restraint, but grew insolent on imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 自以酬賞既極，便情在無上，刑戮逆濫，政用暴苛。

translations.literal: Thinking his rewards and appointments had reached their limit, his will turned to what lay above all; punishments and executions were perverse and excessive, and government was harsh and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced he had been rewarded to the full, he set his heart on what lay above the throne: executions ran wild, and his rule turned savage and severe.

sentences.zh: 問鼎之迹日彰，人臣之禮頓缺。

translations.literal: Day by day the traces of asking about the cauldron grew plain, and the rites owed by a minister suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Each day his designs on the throne grew clearer, and the deference owed a subject was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 陛下四時膳御，觸事縣空，宮省供奉，十不一在。

translations.literal: Your Majestys meals through the four seasons, whenever touched upon were vacant; of the palace and departmental provisions, not one in ten remained.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majestys table through the four seasons stood bare at every turn; not one in ten of the palace supplies remained.

sentences.zh: 皇后寢疾之際，湯藥不周，手與家書，多所求告。

translations.literal: When the Empress lay ill in bed, broths and medicines were not complete; he wrote family letters by hand with many demands and requests.
translations.idiomatic: While the Empress lay sick, medicines went wanting; he sent private letters by hand, piling demand upon demand.

sentences.zh: 皆是朝士共所聞見，莫不傷懷憤歎，口不敢言。

translations.literal: These were all things that court gentlemen together had seen and heard; none was not wounded in heart and indignant with sighs, yet dared not speak with their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Every courtier had seen and heard these things; all grieved and seethed in silence, afraid to speak aloud.

sentences.zh: 前揚州刺史元顯第五息法興，桓玄之釁，逃遠於外，王路既開，始得歸本。

translations.literal: The fifth son Faming of former Governor of Yangzhou Yuan Xian, in the turmoil of Huan Xuan, fled far abroad; once the royal road was opened, he at last could return to his roots.
translations.idiomatic: Faming, fifth son of the former Yangzhou governor Yuan Xian, had fled abroad during Huan Xuans rebellion; when the lawful order was restored, he was at last able to come home.

sentences.zh: 太傅之胤，絕而復興，凡在有懷，誰不感慶。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Grand Tutor, cut off then revived—as to all who cherish good faith, who would not be moved to rejoice?
translations.idiomatic: A scion of the Grand Tutor, a house extinguished and brought back to life—who among loyal hearts could fail to rejoice?

sentences.zh: 裕吞噬之心，不避輕重，以法興聰敏明慧，必為民望所歸，芳蘭既茂，內懷憎惡，乃妄扇異言，無罪即戮。

translations.literal: Yus devouring heart did not shun light or heavy; thinking Faming clever and bright and sure to become what the peoples hopes turned to, the fragrant orchid already flourishing, he bore hatred within and therefore groundlessly stirred contrary talk—and without guilt immediately executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yus appetite for destruction spared neither great nor small. Faming was clever and beloved by the people; Liu Yu saw talent like a blooming orchid and hated it in secret. He spread false charges and executed an innocent man.

sentences.zh: 大司馬臣德文及王妃公主，情計切逼，並狼狽請命。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, Minister De Wen, and the princesses of royal consort rank—their feelings and plans pressed to extremity—all in distress pleaded for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Sima Dewen, the consorts, and the princesses were driven to desperation and all pleaded for mercy.

sentences.zh: 逆肆禍毒，誓不矜許，寃酷之痛，感動行路。

translations.literal: The rebel wantonly displayed poisonous harm and swore not to show pity or assent; the pain of wrongful cruelty moved travelers on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The usurpers cruelty knew no mercy; the agony of his injustice wrung tears even from passersby on the road.

sentences.zh: 自以地卑位重，荷恩崇大，乃以庶孽與德文嫡婚，致茲非偶，實由威逼。

translations.literal: Thinking himself low in standing yet heavy in position, bearing grace raised high, he therefore married a son born of a concubine to De Wens legitimate daughter, causing this ill-matched union—truly by intimidation and force.
translations.idiomatic: Humble in birth yet exalted in rank, he forced a marriage between his bastard son and Sima Dewens legitimate daughter—a grotesque match wholly compelled by power.

sentences.zh: 故衞將軍劉毅、右將軍劉藩、前將軍諸葛長民、尚書僕射謝混、南蠻校尉郗僧施，或盛勳德胤，令望在身，皆社稷輔弼，協讚所寄，無罪無辜，一旦夷滅。

translations.literal: Formerly Guard General Liu Yi, Right General Liu Fan, Vanguard General Zhuge Changmin, Master of Writing Xie Hun, and Commandant of Southern Man Xi Shengshi—some with flourishing merits and virtues heirs, commanding prestige in their persons—all were pillars assisting the altars of state, the co-support on which reliance was placed; without guilt, without crime, in a single day exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Guard General Liu Yi, Right General Liu Fan, Vanguard General Zhuge Changmin, Master of Writing Xie Hun, and Southern Man Commandant Xi Shengshi—men of towering merit and public esteem, pillars of the realm—all were slaughtered in a day without charge or crime.

sentences.zh: 猜忍之性，終古所希。

translations.literal: A suspicious and cruel nature such as this has rarely been seen since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion and cruelty such as his are almost unknown in all of history.

sentences.zh: 臣自惟門戶衰破，賴之獲存，皇家所重，終古難匹。

translations.literal: I myself reflect that my house was decayed and broken, and by relying on him obtained survival; what the royal house esteems is hard to match through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: My own house had been brought low; I survived only through his protection. The dynastys regard for my line is something few families have ever known.

sentences.zh: 是以公私歸馮，事盡祗順。

translations.literal: Therefore in public and private I turned to him, and in affairs did all reverent compliance.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason I gave him my loyalty in every public and private matter.

sentences.zh: 再授荊州，輒苦陳告，自以才弱位隆，不宜久荷分陝，屢求解任，必不見聽。

translations.literal: When again assigned Jingzhou, I repeatedly lodged bitter statements, thinking myself weak in talent yet lofty in position, unfit to long bear the divided Shan mandate, many times seeking release from office, yet certainly not permitted to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou was offered me again, I pleaded earnestly that my gifts were slight and my rank too high, that I should not long bear so great a frontier command. Time after time I asked to be relieved, and each time he refused.

sentences.zh: 前經攜侍老母，半家俱西，凡諸子姪，悉留京輦。

translations.literal: Previously I went west taking my aged mother to serve her, half the household together west; all my sons and nephews were left in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when I went west with my aged mother, half my family went with me while all my sons and nephews were left behind in the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣兄子譙王文思，雖年少常人，粗免咎悔，性好交遊，未知防遠，羣醜交構，為其風聲。

translations.literal: My elder brothers son, Prince of Qiao Wen Si, though young was like other men, broadly free of blame and regret, by nature fond of companionship, not knowing how to guard against distance; a swarm of villains intertwined plots, making him a name on the wind.
translations.idiomatic: My brothers son Sima Wensi, prince of Qiao, was young but no worse than other men. He loved company and did not know caution. Villains whispered together until his name was blackened on every wind.

sentences.zh: 裕遂翦戮人士，遠送文思。

translations.literal: Yu then cut down and executed gentlemen and sent Wen Si far away.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu seized scholars and exiles and banished Wensi to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 臣順其此旨，表送章節，請廢文思，改襲大宗，遣息文寶送女東歸。

translations.literal: I complied with this intent and memorialized sending the stamp and cord, asking to depose Wen Si and change the succession to the great lineage, sending my son Wenbao to escort my daughter east to return.
translations.idiomatic: I bowed to his will: I memorialized to depose Wensi, transfer the succession to the main line, and sent my son Wenbao to bring my daughter home to the east.

sentences.zh: 自謂推誠奉順，理不過此。

translations.literal: I thought that in pushing sincerity and offering compliance, reason could go no further than this.
translations.idiomatic: I believed I had shown good faith and submission as far as any man could.

sentences.zh: 豈意裕苞藏禍心，遂見討伐，加惡文思，構生罪釁。

translations.literal: How could I have expected that Yu harbored a treacherous heart and would then be seen in punitive campaign, heaping further harm on Wen Si and fabricating crimes and transgressions?
translations.idiomatic: I never dreamed Liu Yu hid treason in his breast and would march against me, piling new crimes on Wensi and inventing grounds for war.

sentences.zh: 羣小之言，遠近噂𠴲，而臣純愚，闇信必謂不然。

translations.literal: The talk of petty men spread near and far in noisy slander, yet I, purely stupid, believed in darkness that it surely was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Slanders ran everywhere, yet in my folly I clung to the belief that none of it could be true.

sentences.zh: 尋臣府司馬張茂度狼狽東歸，南平太守檀範之復以此月三日委郡叛逆，尋有審問，東軍已上。

translations.literal: Soon my prefectures marshal Zhang Maodu returned east in distress; the Administrator of Nanping Tan Fanzhi again on the third day of this month abandoned his commandery in rebellion; soon there were inquiries, and the eastern army had marched.
translations.idiomatic: Soon my chief clerk Zhang Maodu fled east in disorder. On the third of this month Nanping governor Tan Fanzhi abandoned his post in revolt. Investigations followed, and Liu Yus eastern host was already on the march.

sentences.zh: 裕今此舉，非有怨憎，正以臣王室之幹，位居藩岳，時賢既盡，唯臣獨存，規以翦滅，成其篡殺。

translations.literal: Yus present action has no personal hatred; he is simply because I am the trunk of the royal house, occupying a frontier mountain position; the worthy of the age are already exhausted, only I alone remain—his plot is to cut me down and complete his usurpation and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yus campaign is not born of private spite. I am a pillar of the imperial clan and a great frontier lord; the worthy men of our time are dead, and I alone remain. He intends to cut me down and finish his path to usurpation.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍臣宗之、青州刺史臣敬宣，並是裕所深忌憚，欲以次除蕩，然後傾移天日，於事可易。

translations.literal: Pacifying-north General Zongzhi and Governor of Qingzhou Jingxuan are both men whom Yu deeply fears and dreads; he wishes to eliminate them in turn, and afterward to overturn the sun and sky—then the matter will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-north General Zongzhi and Qingzhou governor Jingxuan are both men Liu Yu deeply dreads. He means to destroy us one by one, then shift the sky itself—and only then will his task be easy.

sentences.zh: 今荊、雍義徒，不召而集，子來之眾，其會如林。

translations.literal: Now the righteous followers of Jing and Yong gather without being summoned; a host that comes like sons, their assembly like a forest.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal men of Jing and Yong are rallying without a summons; soldiers flock to my banners like sons coming home, thick as a forest.

sentences.zh: 豈臣無德所能綏致，蓋七廟之靈，理貫幽顯。

translations.literal: How could it be that without virtue I could pacify and bring them? It is rather the spirit of the seven temples—the principle that penetrates hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: It is not my virtue that draws them. The spirits of the ancestral shrines join the seen and the unseen in one cause.

sentences.zh: 輒授文思振武將軍、南郡太守，宗之子竟陵太守魯軌進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: I have forthwith appointed Wen Si General Who Reanimates Martiality and Administrator of Nanjun; Zongzhis son Lu Gui, Administrator of Jingling, is advanced in title to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: I have appointed Wensi General Who Reanimates Martiality and governor of Nanjun; Zongzhis son Lu Gui, governor of Jingling, is promoted to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 臣今與宗之親御大眾，出據江津，案甲抗威，隨宜應赴。

translations.literal: I now, with Zongzhi, personally lead the great host forth to hold the Yangtze fords, set armor and resist with majesty, responding wherever need calls.
translations.idiomatic: I and Zongzhi will lead the main force to the Yangtze crossings, armor set and banners raised, ready to meet him wherever he strikes.

sentences.zh: 今絳旗所指，唯裕兄弟父子而已。

translations.literal: Now where the crimson banners point, it is only Yu and his brothers and father and sons.
translations.idiomatic: My crimson banners aim only at Liu Yu and his kin, father and sons, brothers all.

sentences.zh: 須剋蕩寇逆，尋續馳聞。

translations.literal: When we must overcome and sweep away the bandit rebels, I will promptly send word again.
translations.idiomatic: When the traitors are crushed, I will send word at once.

sentences.zh: 由臣輕弱，致裕凌橫，上慚俯愧，無以厝顏。

translations.literal: Because I am light and weak, causing Yus overbearing insolence, upward I am ashamed and bow in guilt—there is no way to set my face.
translations.idiomatic: My own weakness has let Liu Yu run rampant. I bow my head in shame before Your Majesty and scarcely dare lift my eyes.

sentences.zh: 休之府錄事參軍韓延之，故吏也，有幹用才能。

translations.literal: Xiuzhis Aide-de-Camp Han Yanzhi was a former subordinate, with capacity and talents for practical achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, registrar on Xiuzhis staff, had been Liu Yus old officer—a man of energy and ability.

sentences.zh: 公未至江陵，密使與之書曰：「文思事源，遠近所知，去秋遣康之送還司馬君者，[6]推至公之極也。

translations.literal: Before the Duke had reached Jiangling, he secretly sent someone to write to him, saying: "The source of the Wen Si affair is known near and far; last autumn sending Kangzhi to escort back the Lord of Sima was pushing favor to your utmost limit."
translations.idiomatic: Before Liu Yu reached Jiangling, he secretly sent him a letter: "The affair of Wensi is known far and wide. Last autumn, when I sent Kangzhi to return him to you, I was yielding to you to the utmost."

sentences.zh: 而了不遜愧，又無表疏。

translations.literal: Yet there was completely no yielding shame, and again no memorial or communication.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he showed no remorse, and never submitted a memorial of explanation.

sentences.zh: 文思經正不反，此是天地之不容。

translations.literal: Wen Si, having passed through correction, did not return—this is what Heaven and Earth cannot tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: Wensi, having been corrected once, refused to return—that is what Heaven and Earth cannot abide.

sentences.zh: 吾受命西討，止其父子而已。

translations.literal: I have received the mandate to campaign west; it stops at his father and sons, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: I have been commanded to march west; my quarrel is with father and son alone.

sentences.zh: 彼土僑舊，為所驅逼，一無所問。

translations.literal: The sojourning veterans of that land, driven and compelled by him—none shall be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: The migrants and old retainers of that region, forced into this, shall not be questioned at all.

sentences.zh: 往年郗僧施、謝邵、任集之等，交構積歲，專為劉毅謀主，所以至此。

translations.literal: In former years Xi Shengshi, Xie Shao, Ren Jizhi, and others wove plots through accumulated years, devoted as chief plotters for Liu Yi—that is why it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: For years Xi Shengshi, Xie Shao, Ren Jizhi, and the rest plotted on Liu Yis behalf. That is how things came to this pass.

sentences.zh: 卿等諸人，一時逼迫，本無纖釁。

translations.literal: You gentlemen and the rest, compelled for a time, originally had no thread of offense.
translations.idiomatic: You were pressed into service for a season; you yourselves bore no smallest fault.

sentences.zh: 吾處懷期物，自有由來。

translations.literal: My disposition in embracing and awaiting worthy men has reasons that go back to their source.
translations.idiomatic: My habit of meeting men with an open heart has old roots.

sentences.zh: 今在近路，正是諸人歸身之日。

translations.literal: Now on the near road is precisely the day for you gentlemen to return yourselves to loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I am on the road now; today is the day for you to come back to me.

sentences.zh: 若大軍登道，交鋒接刃，蘭艾吾誠不分。

translations.literal: If the great army mounts the road and clash meets blade edge, orchid and mugwort—I truly shall not distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: If my host meets yours blade to blade, I swear I shall not tell fragrant orchid from common mugwort.

sentences.zh: 故具示意，并示同懷諸人。

translations.literal: Therefore I fully set forth my intent, and also show it to the like-minded among you.
translations.idiomatic: I set all this out plainly—show it to all who share your hearts.

sentences.zh: 」延之報曰：

translations.literal: " Yanzhi replied, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Han Yanzhi answered:

sentences.zh: 承親率戎馬，遠履西畿，闔境士庶，莫不恇駭。

translations.literal: I learn that you personally lead war horses and far tread the western capital region; the gentlemen and commoners of the whole territory are none not terrified and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: I learn that you are leading your army in person deep into the western heartland. Every gentleman and commoner in these parts is struck with fear.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 莫知師出之名故也。

translations.literal: None know the name or reason for which the army marches forth.
translations.idiomatic: No one knows the name—the stated cause—of this campaign.

sentences.zh: 今辱來疏，始知以譙王前事，良增歎息。

translations.literal: Now, shamed by your letter arriving, I at last know it is because of the Prince of Qiaos former affair—truly this increases sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter, humbling as it is to receive, tells me the march is over the prince of Qiaos affair. That deepens my grief.

sentences.zh: 司馬平西體國忠貞，欵愛待物，當於古人中求耳。

translations.literal: Sima Pacifier-of-the-West embodied the states loyalty and sincerity, treated men with sincere affection—one must seek such among the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifier-of-the-West Sima embodied loyalty to the state and treated men with good faith. You must look to antiquity for his like.

sentences.zh: 以君公有匡復之勳，家國蒙賴，推德委誠，每事詢仰。

translations.literal: Because you, my lord, have the merit of restoring the realm and the house and state rely on you, he extended virtue and entrusted sincerity, in every affair consulting and looking up to you.
translations.idiomatic: Because you restored the realm, the dynasty owes you its life. He extended you his trust and looked to you in every matter.

sentences.zh: 譙王往以微事見劾，猶自表遜位；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao in the past was impeached on a slight matter, yet still memorialized yielding his position;
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qiao was charged once for a trifle, yet he still memorialized to yield his rank.

sentences.zh: 況以大過而當默然邪。

translations.literal: How much more for a great fault—should he have been silent?
translations.idiomatic: How then could he keep silent when charged with so grave an offense?

sentences.zh: 但康之前言有所不盡，故重使胡道諮白所懷。

translations.literal: Only Kangzhis former words did not fully exhaust the matter; therefore I again sent Hu Daozi to speak forth what was in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhis first message did not say all; therefore I sent Hu Daozi again to lay my mind bare.

sentences.zh: 道未及反，已奏表廢之，所不盡者命耳。

translations.literal: Daozi had not yet returned when the memorial to depose him was already submitted—what was not exhausted was fate alone.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi had not yet returned when you had already memorialized to depose him. What was left unsaid was fate, not your patience.

sentences.zh: 推寄相與之懷，正當如此？

translations.literal: Is this how you should honor the trust mutually placed?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how you honor the trust between you?

sentences.zh: 有何不可，便興兵戈。

translations.literal: What could not be accommodated—yet weapons of war were raised?
translations.idiomatic: What could not be settled that you must take up arms?

sentences.zh: 自義旗秉權以來，四方方伯，誰敢不先相諮疇，而逕表天子邪。

translations.literal: Since the righteous banner wielded power, of the regional lords in the four directions—who dared not first consult together before directly memorializing the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Since the righteous standard was raised, which regional lord has dared report straight to the throne without conferring with his peers first?

sentences.zh: 譙王為宰相所責，又表廢之，經正何歸，表使何因，可謂「欲加之罪，其無辭乎」！

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao was reproached by the chief minister, and again a memorial was made to depose him—where did correction go, what cause did the memorial serve? One may say, "He who wishes to add guilt to a man will never lack words!"
translations.idiomatic: Blamed by the chief minister, the prince was memorialized for deposition—where was the correction, what was the memorials ground? It is truly "when you wish to saddle a man with guilt, no words are wanting."

sentences.zh: 劉裕足下，海內之人，誰不見足下此心，而復欲欺誑國士！

translations.literal: Liu Yu beneath your feet—of men within the seas, who does not see this heart of yours, yet you still wish to deceive the nations gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu—all the world sees your heart, and still you would deceive men of honor!

sentences.zh: 天地所不容，在彼不在此矣。

translations.literal: What Heaven and Earth cannot tolerate lies on that side, not on this.
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven and Earth cannot tolerate is on your side, not on ours.

sentences.zh: 來示言「處懷期物，自有由來」。

translations.literal: Your instruction came saying, "My disposition in embracing and awaiting worthy men has reasons that go back to their source."
translations.idiomatic: You wrote that "my habit of meeting men with an open heart has old roots."

sentences.zh: 今伐人之君，啗人以利，真可謂「處懷期物，自有由來」者矣。

translations.literal: Now attacking another mans lord and feeding men with profit—this may truly be called "embracing and awaiting worthy men with reasons from their source"!
translations.idiomatic: Now you march against another mans lord and bait men with profit—that is your "open heart with old roots"!

sentences.zh: 劉藩死於閶闔之內，諸葛斃於左右之手，甘言詫方伯，襲之以輕兵，遂使席上靡款懷之士，閫外無自信諸侯，以是為得算，良可恥也。

translations.literal: Liu Fan died within the Gate of Heaven, Zhuge perished by hands at ones side; sweet words flattered the regional lords, and light troops attacked them—thus making on the mat no gentlemen of sincere hearts, beyond the gate no self-confident feudal lords; to think this winning calculation is truly shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan died within the palace gates. Zhuge Changmin was struck down at your side. Soft words won the lords, then light troops struck; no man at court dares open his heart, no lord beyond the passes trusts his own strength. To call this sound strategy is shame itself.

sentences.zh: 貴府將佐及朝廷賢德，寄性命以過日，心企太平久矣。

translations.literal: The staff and assistants of your honorable mansion and the worthy and virtuous of the court entrust their lives to pass the days; long they have looked in heart to great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your staff and the worthy men of the court stake their lives day to day, longing for peace.

sentences.zh: 吾誠鄙劣，嘗聞道於君子。

translations.literal: I am truly base and inferior, yet once heard the Way from a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: I am a coarse man, but I have heard the Way taught by gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 以平西之至德，寧可無授命之臣乎！

translations.literal: With Pacifier-of-the-Wests utmost virtue, how could there fail to be ministers who received mandate?
translations.idiomatic: With virtue such as Pacifier-of-the-Wests, will there be no men who hold to their charge?

sentences.zh: 未能自投虎口，比迹郗、任之徒明矣。

translations.literal: That I could not throw myself into the tigers maw—compared with the traces of Xi and Ren, it is clear.
translations.idiomatic: I will not throw myself into the tigers mouth like Xi Shengshi and Ren Jizhi—that much is clear.

sentences.zh: 假令天長喪亂，九流渾濁，當與臧洪遊於地下，不復多言。

translations.literal: If Heaven lengthens chaos and the nine currents muddle, I shall wander underground with Zang Hong—no more many words.
translations.idiomatic: Should Heaven prolong these evil days and the world run foul, I shall keep company underground with Zang Hong, and say no more.

sentences.zh: 公視書歎息，以示諸佐曰：「事人當如此。」

translations.literal: The Duke looked at the letter and sighed, showing it to his assistants, saying: "To serve another should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu read the letter, sighed, and showed it to his staff. "This is how one should serve a lord," he said.

sentences.zh: 三月，軍次江陵。

translations.literal: In the third month, the army halted at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the army reached Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初雍州刺史魯宗之常慮不為公所容，與休之相結，至是率其子竟陵太守軌會于江陵。

translations.literal: Initially Yongzhou Governor Lu Zongzhi often feared he would not be tolerated by the Duke, and bonded with Xiuzhi; at this time he led his son Jingling Governor Gui to meet at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yongzhou governor Lu Zongzhi had feared Liu Yu would not spare him and had allied with Xiuzhi. Now he led his son Lu Gui, governor of Jingling, to join him at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 江夏太守劉虔之邀之，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: Jiangxia Governor Liu Qianzhi intercepted them; the army was defeated and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia governor Liu Qianzhi moved to block them; his force was defeated and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 公命彭城內史徐逵之、參軍王允之出江夏口，復為軌所敗，並沒。

translations.literal: The Duke ordered Pengcheng Administrator Xu Daizhi and aide Wang Yunzhi out through Jiangxia pass; they were again defeated by Gui, both perished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Pengcheng administrator Xu Daizhi and aide Wang Yunzhi through the Jiangxia crossing; Lu Gui defeated them again and both were lost.

sentences.zh: 時公軍泊馬頭，即日率眾軍濟江，躬督諸將登岸，莫不奮踊爭先。

translations.literal: At that time the Dukes army moored at Matou; that very day he led the host across the river, personally directing the generals ashore; none did not spring forward striving to be first.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yus army was moored at Matou. That same day he led the host across the river and personally directed the landing; every man strove to be first ashore.

sentences.zh: 休之眾潰，與軌等奔襄陽，江陵平。

translations.literal: Xiuzhis forces collapsed; with Gui and others he fled to Xiangyang; Jiangling was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhis army broke; he fled with Gui and the rest to Xiangyang. Jiangling was pacified.

sentences.zh: 加領南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed to head the Southern Man Commandantcy.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Commandant of Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 將拜，值四廢日，佐史鄭鮮之、褚叔度、王弘、傅亮白遷日，不許。

translations.literal: When he was about to be appointed, it fell on a four-defilement day; aides Zheng Xianzhi, Chu Shudu, Wang Hong, and Fu Liang reported changing the day; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When he was to take up office, the day fell among the four defilements. His aides Zheng Xianzhi, Chu Shudu, Wang Hong, and Fu Liang asked that the date be moved; permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「此州積弊，事故相仍，民疲田蕪，杼軸空匱。

translations.literal: His order went down: "This province has accumulated abuses; calamities follow one another; the people are weary, fields lie waste, the looms axle is empty in storehouses."
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "This province bears deep abuses; disasters follow one upon another. The people are exhausted, fields lie fallow, and the storehouses are bare."

sentences.zh: 加以舊章乖昧，事役頻苦，童耄奪養，老稚服戎，空戶從役，或越紼應召。

translations.literal: Added to this, old regulations are obscure and confused, corvée labor frequent and bitter; children and aged are torn from their nurture, the old and young bear arms; empty households meet service, some cross mourning shades to answer summons.
translations.idiomatic: Old rules are tangled and service is crushing: infants and elders are torn from their homes, the old and young are pressed into arms. Empty households are levied for labor; some are called up before mourning is done.

sentences.zh: 每永懷民瘼，宵分忘寢，誠宜蠲除苛政，弘茲簡惠。

translations.literal: Every time I long cherish the peoples afflictions and at midnight forget sleep—truly it is fitting to remove harsh government and spread this simplicity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When I think of the peoples suffering I cannot sleep past midnight. Harsh rule must be lifted and simple kindness spread abroad.

sentences.zh: 庶令凋風弊政，與事而新，寧一之化，成於朞月。

translations.literal: I hope to make declining customs and bad government, with the affairs, made new; the transformation of peaceful unity accomplished within a full month.
translations.idiomatic: May ruined customs and corrupt government be made new with these measures, and tranquil order achieved within a single month.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍二州，西局、蠻府吏及軍人年十二以還，六十以上，及扶養孤幼，單丁大艱，悉仰遣之。

translations.literal: Jing and Yong two provinces, Western Bureau and Man-office clerks and soldiers aged twelve and under, sixty and above, and those supporting orphans and the young, sole heirs with great hardship—all are ordered dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing and Yong, clerks of the western bureau and the Man office, and soldiers twelve or younger or sixty or older, and all who support orphans or the young, or sole heirs in grave hardship—all are to be sent home.

sentences.zh: 窮獨不能存者，給其長賑。

translations.literal: Those poor and alone who cannot survive, grant them long-term relief.
translations.idiomatic: Those destitute and alone who cannot live are to receive long relief grain.

sentences.zh: 府州久勤將吏，依勞銓序。

translations.literal: Prefecture and province long-serving officers and clerks, according to labor assign rank and order.
translations.idiomatic: Long-serving officers and clerks of the prefecture and province are to be ranked according to their service.

sentences.zh: 并除今年租稅。」

translations.literal: And remit this years land tax and levies."
translations.idiomatic: This years taxes and levies are remitted."

sentences.zh: 四月，公復率眾進討，至襄陽，休之奔羌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Duke again led the host forward in campaign to Xiangyang; Xiuzhi fled to the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Liu Yu led his army forward again to Xiangyang. Xiuzhi fled to the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 天子復重申前命，授太傅、揚州牧，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，加前部羽葆、鼓吹，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again solemnly reiterated the former commands, appointing Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, sword and shoes in the hall, not hurrying in court audience, praise and bow without naming the name, adding front guard of feather parasols and musical procession, establishing left and right Chief Clerks, Marshals, and Attending Gentlemen four men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again confirmed the earlier appointments: Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with sword and shoes in the hall, no need to hurry in audience, praise and bow without naming his name, plus the front guard of feather parasols and drums, and four posts each of chief clerk, marshal, and attending gentleman on left and right.

sentences.zh: 封公第三子義隆為北彭城縣公。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the Dukes third son Yilong as Duke of Northern Pengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Yilong was enfeoffed as Duke of Northern Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍道憐為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He made Central Army General Daolian Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army general Daolian was made governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月甲子，公至自江陵，奉還黃鉞，固辭太傅、州牧、前部羽葆、鼓吹，其餘受命。

translations.literal: On jiazi in the eighth month, the Duke arrived from Jiangling, returned the yellow battle-axe, firmly declined Grand Tutor, provincial governorship, front feather parasols and musical procession; the rest of the commands he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the eighth month Liu Yu returned from Jiangling. He gave back the yellow battle-axe and firmly declined Grand Tutor, the provincial governorship, and the front parasols and drums; he accepted the rest.

sentences.zh: 朝議以公道尊勳重，不宜復施敬護軍，既加殊禮，奏事不復稱名。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that the Dukes Way was honored and merit heavy—he should not again be shown the respect of Protector of the Army; since exceptional rites were added, in memorials he would no longer be called by name.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that his merit and standing were too great for him still to show deference to the Protector of the Army. With these extraordinary honors granted, memorials no longer used his personal name.

sentences.zh: 以世子為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He made the heir Prince Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，詔公依舊辟士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, first month, an edict ordered the Duke to recruit gentlemen as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year an edict allowed him to recruit staff as before.

sentences.zh: 加領平北將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Additional appointment as Pacifying-north General and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Pacifying-north General and governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 增都督南秦，凡二十二州。

translations.literal: His supervision was increased to include Southern Qin—in all twenty-two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His area of command was extended to Southern Qin, twenty-two provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 公以平北文武寡少，不宜別置。

translations.literal: The Duke thought the Pacifying-north civil and military staff were few and should not be separately established.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu held that the Pacifying-north staff were too few to warrant a separate establishment.

sentences.zh: 於是罷平北府，以併大府。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abolished the Pacifying-north headquarters and merged it into the Grand headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the Pacifying-north headquarters and merged it with his main command.

sentences.zh: 以世子為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He made the heir Prince Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，加公中外大都督。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Duke was advanced to Grand Commander of Court and Country.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was made Grand Commander of Court and Country.

sentences.zh: 初公平齊，仍有定關、洛之意，值盧循侵逼，故其事不諧。

translations.literal: When first he had pacified Qi, he still had the intent to settle the Passes and Luoyang; it happened that Lu Xun pressed in attack, and therefore the matter did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Qi he still meant to recover the passes and Luoyang, but Lu Xuns rebellion forced him to set that plan aside.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍既平，方謀外略。

translations.literal: Jing and Yong being already pacified, he then plotted outward expansion.
translations.idiomatic: With Jing and Yong secure, he turned to campaigns beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 會羌主姚興死，子泓立，兄弟相殺，關中擾亂，公乃戒嚴北討。

translations.literal: It happened that the Qiang ruler Yao Xing died, his son Hong established himself, brothers killed one another, and Guanzhong was thrown into turmoil; the Duke then ordered the army on alert for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing of the Qiang died; his son Hong took the throne while brothers slaughtered one another and Guanzhong fell into chaos. Gaozu ordered the army to mobilize for a northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 加領征西將軍、司豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Campaigning-west General and Governor of the two provinces Si and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Campaigning-west General and governor of Si and Yu.

sentences.zh: 以世子為徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: He made the heir Prince Governor of the two provinces Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made governor of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「吾倡大義，首自本州，克復皇祚，遂建勳烈，外夷勍敵，內清姦軌，皆邦人州黨竭誠盡力之效也。

translations.literal: His order went down: "I raised the great cause first from my home province, recovered the imperial succession, and thus built merit and achievement; foreign barbarians as fierce enemies, and within the realm traitorous paths—all were the effect of fellow countrymen and provincial kin devoting heart and strength to the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "I raised the righteous cause in my own province, restored the dynasty, and built these achievements. Fierce foes abroad and traitors within were overcome only because the men of our land gave their utmost loyalty."

sentences.zh: 情若風霜，義貫金石。

translations.literal: Feeling like wind and frost, righteousness penetrating metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: My feeling is cold as frost; my duty cuts to the bone.

sentences.zh: 今當奉辭西斾，有事關、河，弱嗣叨蒙，復忝今授，情事纏綿，可謂深矣。

translations.literal: Now I am to take leave with the western banners and have business in the Passes and the Yellow River; the weak heir presumptuously receives favor, again bearing the present appointment—affairs and feelings tangled together, one may say it is deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Now I march west toward the passes and the Yellow River. My young heir has been given this charge again—the ties bind deep indeed.

sentences.zh: 頃軍國務殷，刑辟未息，眷言懷之，能不多歎。

translations.literal: Recently military and state affairs have been pressing, punishments and executions not yet ceased; whenever I speak of it in remembrance, how can I not sigh greatly?
translations.idiomatic: Lately state and army affairs have pressed hard and executions have not ceased. When I think of it, how can I not sigh?

sentences.zh: 其犯罪繫五歲以還，可一原遣。

translations.literal: Those whose crimes warrant imprisonment for five years and back may all once be pardoned and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners sentenced to five years or less are to be pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 文武勞滿未蒙榮轉者，便隨班序報。」

translations.literal: Civil and military men whose labor was full yet who had not received honored promotion should at once be reported according to roster order.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers whose service is complete but who have not yet been promoted are to be reported in roster order.

sentences.zh: 公受中外都督及司州，並辭大司馬琅邪王禮敬，朝議從之。

translations.literal: The Duke received the Commander of Court and Country and the province of Si, and both declined the ceremonial respect owed to the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye; court discussion followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the posts of Commander of Court and Country and governor of Si, but declined the ceremonial deference owed to Grand Marshal Sima of Langye; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 公欲以義聲懷遠，奉琅邪王北伐。

translations.literal: The Duke wished with righteous renown to embrace the distant, and to lead the Prince of Langye on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to win the distant lands by righteous fame and to conduct the northern campaign in the name of the Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 五月，羌偽黃門侍郎尹沖率兄弟歸順。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the false Qiang Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yin Chong led his brothers in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yin Chong, false Qiang Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, led his brothers in surrender.

sentences.zh: 又加公北雍州刺史，前部羽葆、鼓吹，增班劍為四十人。

translations.literal: He was again advanced as Governor of Northern Yongzhou, with front guard of feather parasols and musical procession, and ceremonial swords increased to forty.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made governor of Northern Yongzhou, with front parasols and drums and forty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 解中書監。

translations.literal: He was released from Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned the post of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 八月丁巳，率大眾發京師。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi in the eighth month, he led the great host forth from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day in the eighth month he led the main army out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 以世子為中軍將軍，監太尉留府事。

translations.literal: He made the heir Prince Central Army General, supervising the Grand Commandants retained headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made Central Army General and left to supervise the Grand Commandants headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射劉穆之為左僕射，領監軍、中軍二府軍司，入居東府，總攝內外。

translations.literal: Master of Writing, Right Vice Director Liu Muzhi was made Left Vice Director, heading supervision of the Army and Central Army headquarters as army clerks, entering to reside in the Eastern Headquarters, overseeing all within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, became Left Vice Director, supervising the Army and Central Army headquarters, moved into the Eastern Headquarters, and oversaw affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 九月，公次于彭城，加領徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Duke halted at Pengcheng and was additionally appointed Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he halted at Pengcheng and was additionally made governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡步向許、洛，羌緣道屯守，皆望風降服。

translations.literal: Earlier he had sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Flying-dragon General Wang Zhen’e on foot toward Xu and Luoyang; Qiang along the road garrisoned and held, all looked to the wind and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen’e toward Xu and Luoyang on foot; Qiang garrisons along the route submitted at the first report of his approach.

sentences.zh: 偽兗州刺史韋華先據倉垣，亦率眾歸順。

translations.literal: The false Governor of Yanzhou Wei Hua had first held Cangyuan, and also led his host in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hua, the false governor of Yanzhou, who had held Cangyuan, also surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 公又遣北兗州刺史王仲德先以水軍入河。

translations.literal: The Duke again sent Northern Yanzhou Governor Wang Zhongde first to enter the river with the navy.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu also sent Wang Zhongde, governor of Northern Yanzhou, to lead the fleet into the river first.

sentences.zh: 仲德破索虜於東郡涼城，進平滑臺。

translations.literal: Zhongde defeated the Suolu barbarians at Liangcheng in Dongjun and advanced to pacify Pingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde defeated the Suolu at Liangcheng in Dong commandery and advanced to pacify Pingtai.

sentences.zh: 十月，眾軍至洛陽，圍金墉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the host of armies reached Luoyang and besieged Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the armies reached Luoyang and besieged Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 泓弟偽平南將軍洸請降，送于京師。

translations.literal: Hongs younger brother, the false Pacifying-south General Guang, asked to surrender and was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hong’s younger brother Guang, false Pacifying-south General, surrendered and was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 修復晉五陵，置守衞。

translations.literal: The five tombs of Jin were restored and guards were set.
translations.idiomatic: The five Jin imperial tombs were restored and guards appointed.

sentences.zh: 天子詔曰：

translations.literal: The Son of Heavens edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's edict said:

sentences.zh: 夫嵩、岱配極，則乾道增輝，藩嶽作屏，則帝王成務。

translations.literal: Song and Dai match the pole, then the way of Heaven adds brilliance; frontier mountains serve as screens, then emperors and kings complete their task.
translations.idiomatic: When Song and Dai stand as the cosmic pillars, the Way of Heaven shines brighter; when frontier mountains serve as the royal screen, the work of emperors and kings is fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 是以夏、殷資昆、彭之伯，有周倚齊、晉之輔。

translations.literal: Therefore Xia and Yin relied on the lords Kun and Peng; Zhou had Qi and Jin as assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xia and Yin drew on lords like Kun and Peng; Zhou leaned on Qi and Jin as its supports.

sentences.zh: 鑒諸前典，儀刑萬代，翼治扶危，靡不由此。

translations.literal: Mirroring the former canons, as law and model for ten thousand generations—supporting rule and upholding the endangered, none is not through this.
translations.idiomatic: Looking to the ancient precedents, the model for ten thousand generations: to steady the throne and rescue the imperiled, nothing serves better than this.

sentences.zh: 太尉公命世天縱，齊聖廣淵，明燭四方，道光宇宙。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant, Duke, was by fate of the age Heaven-sent, together sagely and broadly deep, illuminating the four directions, his Way shining through the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant was Heaven-sent for his age, sage and far-reaching, his light falling on the four quarters, his Way filling the universe.

sentences.zh: 爰自□□初迪，則投懃王國，妖蝥孔熾，則功存社稷。

translations.literal: From the beginning of □□, then he devoted his effort to the royal house; when the demon locusts were greatly raging, then his merit lay in preserving the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: From the first stirrings of the righteous restoration he gave himself to the royal house; when ruin threatened the realm, he preserved the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 固以四維是荷，萬邦攸賴者矣。

translations.literal: Thus the four bonds were what he bore, and the ten thousand states relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: The four pillars of the realm rested on him; the myriad states looked to him for support.

sentences.zh: 暨桓玄僭逆，傾蕩四海，公深秉大節，靈武霆震，弘濟朕躬，再造王室。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped and rebelled, overturning and sweeping the four seas, the Duke deeply held the great constancy; his numinous martiality thundered and quaked, broadly saving Our person, again making the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne and shook the four seas, the Duke held fast to the highest loyalty. His martial power thundered forth; he saved Us and remade the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 每惟勳德，銘于厥心，遂北清海、岱，南夷百越，荊、雍稽服，庸、岷順軌，剋黜方難，式遏寇虐。
