translations.literal: Recently when the altars toppled, the King rescued and preserved them; when the central plain lay waste and choked, he crossed and restored it.
translations.idiomatic: When the altars toppled, the King rescued them; when the central plain lay waste, he crossed and restored it.

sentences.zh: 自負固不賓，干紀放命，肆逆滔天，竊據萬里。

translations.literal: From those who relied on their strength and would not submit, who violated the statutes and defied command, who ran riot against Heaven and secretly held ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: From rebels who relied on strength, violated statutes, defied command, ran riot against Heaven, and held vast lands in secret.

sentences.zh: 靡不潤之以風雨，震之以雷霆。

translations.literal: None failed to be moistened with wind and rain, shaken with thunder.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to be moistened with wind and rain and shaken with thunder.

sentences.zh: 九伐之道既敷，八法之化自理。

translations.literal: The nine punitive campaigns were spread abroad; the eight methods of transformation were ordered of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The nine punitive campaigns were spread abroad; the eight methods of rule ordered themselves.

sentences.zh: 豈伊博施於民，濟斯黔庶；

translations.literal: How could it be only that he broadly bestowed upon the people and aided these black-haired folk;
translations.idiomatic: How could it be only that he broadly bestowed on the people and aided the common folk;

sentences.zh: 固以義洽四海，道威八荒者矣。

translations.literal: truly righteousness harmonized the four seas and the Way awed the eight regions.
translations.idiomatic: truly his righteousness harmonized the four seas and his Way awed the eight regions.

sentences.zh: 至於上天垂象，四靈效徵，圖讖之文既明，人神之望已改。

translations.literal: As for Heaven hanging signs, the four numina showing omens, the charts and prophecies already clear, and the hope of men and spirits already changed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hung signs, the four numina showed omens, charts and prophecies were clear, and the hope of men and spirits had changed.

sentences.zh: 百工歌於朝，庶民頌于野，億兆抃踊，傾佇惟新。

translations.literal: The hundred craftsmen sang in court, the common people praised in the fields; the hundred millions leaped for joy, all leaning and waiting for the new.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen sang in court, common people praised in the fields; the millions leaped for joy and waited for the new.

sentences.zh: 自非百姓樂推，天命攸集，豈伊在予，所得獨專。

translations.literal: If not that the people gladly pushed him forward and Heaven’s mandate gathered upon him, how could We alone monopolize it?
translations.idiomatic: If the people had not gladly pushed him forward and Heaven’s mandate gathered upon him, how could We alone hold it?

sentences.zh: 是用仰祗皇靈，俯順羣議，敬禪神器，授帝位于爾躬。

translations.literal: Therefore We respectfully receive the imperial numen, bow to the multitude’s counsel, reverently yield the sacred vessel, and confer the imperial seat upon your person.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We respectfully receive the imperial numen, bow to the multitude’s counsel, reverently yield the sacred vessel, and confer the throne upon you.

sentences.zh: 大祚告窮，天祿永終。

translations.literal: The great succession is announced exhausted; Heaven’s blessing ends forever.
translations.idiomatic: The great succession is exhausted; Heaven’s blessing ends forever.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 王其允執其中，敬遵典訓，副率土之嘉願，恢洪業於無窮，時膺休祐，以答三靈之眷望。

translations.literal: King, hold fast the center, reverently follow the canon and instruction, answer the realm’s glad wish, and expand the great enterprise without end; always receive fine blessing to answer the three spirits’ trusting gaze.
translations.idiomatic: King, hold fast the center, reverently follow the canon, answer the realm’s glad wish, expand the great enterprise without end, and always receive fine blessing to answer the three spirits’ gaze.

sentences.zh: 又璽書曰：

translations.literal: Again the imperial letter said:
translations.idiomatic: Again the imperial letter said:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞天生蒸民，樹之以君，帝皇寄世，實公四海，崇替係於勳德，升降存乎其人。

translations.literal: We have heard that Heaven born the teeming people and set up a ruler for them; emperors and kings entrusted their generations and truly held the four seas; rise and fall depended on merit and virtue, advancement and decline rested on the man.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that Heaven born the teeming people and set up rulers for them; emperors held the four seas; rise and fall depended on merit and virtue, advancement and decline on the man.

sentences.zh: 故有國必亡，卜年著其數，代謝無常，聖哲握其符。

translations.literal: Therefore states must perish; divination fixes their years; succession is without constancy, and the sage grasps the talisman.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore states must perish; divination fixes their years; succession is without constancy, and the sage grasps the mandate.

sentences.zh: 昔在上世，三聖係軌，疇咨四嶽，以弘揖讓。

translations.literal: In high antiquity the three sages followed in track; they consulted the four peaks to enlarge abdication.
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity the three sages followed in track and consulted the four peaks to enlarge abdication.

sentences.zh: 惟先王之有作，永垂範於無窮。

translations.literal: Only when the former kings made their mark did they hang a model without end.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the former kings acted did they hang a model without end.

sentences.zh: 及劉氏致禪，實堯是法，有魏告終，亦憲茲典。

translations.literal: When the Liu house abdicated, it truly took Yao as its model; when Wei announced its end, it likewise followed this canon.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu house abdicated, it took Yao as its model; when Wei ended, it followed the same canon.

sentences.zh: 我世祖所以撫歸運而順人事，乘利見而定天保者也。

translations.literal: Our founding emperor therefore soothed the returning fortune and complied with human affairs, riding the favorable sign to fix Heaven’s protection.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding emperor soothed the returning fortune, complied with human affairs, and rode the favorable sign to fix Heaven’s protection.

sentences.zh: 而道不常泰，戎夷亂華，喪我洛食，蹙國江表，仍遘否運，淪沒相因。

translations.literal: Yet the Way was not always at peace; barbarians disturbed China; We lost the Luoyang sacrifice and the state was cramped south of the river; again We met ill fortune, and ruin followed ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Way was not always at peace; barbarians disturbed China; We lost Luoyang and the state was cramped south of the river; ill fortune followed ruin upon ruin.

sentences.zh: 逮于元興，遂傾宗祀。

translations.literal: Down to the Yuanxing era the ancestral sacrifices toppled.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yuanxing era the ancestral sacrifices had toppled.

sentences.zh: 幸賴神武光天，大節宏發，匡復我社稷，重造我國家。

translations.literal: Fortunately relying on divine martial brilliance that overspread Heaven, the great constancy broadly rose, We restored Our altars and remade Our state.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately, relying on divine martial brilliance that overspread Heaven, the great constancy rose, We restored Our altars and remade Our state.

sentences.zh: 惟王聖德欽明，則天光大，應期誕載，明保王室。

translations.literal: Only the King’s sagely virtue is reverent and bright; he mirrors Heaven and his radiance is great; he answered the term and was born to carry it; he clearly protected the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Only the King’s sagely virtue is reverent and bright; he mirrors Heaven with great radiance; born to the term, he clearly protected the royal house.

sentences.zh: 內紓國難，外播宏略，誅太憝於漢陽，逋僭盜於沂渚，澄氛西岷，肅清南越，再靜江、湘，拓定樊、沔。

translations.literal: Within he eased the state’s hardship, without he spread the grand design; he executed the great villain at Hanyang, drove off the usurping robber at Yizhu, cleared the mists west of Min, swept the south of Yue, again quieted the Yangtze and Xiang, and opened and settled Fan and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Within he eased the state’s hardship, without he spread the grand design; he executed the great villain at Hanyang, drove off usurpers at Yizhu, cleared the west, swept the south, again quieted the Yangtze and Xiang, and settled Fan and Mian.

sentences.zh: 若乃永懷區宇，思一聲教，王師首路，則伊、洛澄流，稜威崤、潼，則華嶽褰靄，偽酋銜璧，咸陽即序。

translations.literal: As for forever embracing the realm and desiring one sound of teaching—when the royal army took the road, then Yi and Luo ran clear; when majesty reached Xia and Tong, then Mount Hua lifted its mist; false chiefs offered their jade, and Xianyang at once took order.
translations.idiomatic: Forever embracing the realm and desiring one teaching—when the royal army marched, Yi and Luo ran clear; when majesty reached the passes, Mount Hua lifted its mist; false rulers offered jade, and Xianyang submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 雖彝器所銘，詩書所詠，庸勳之盛，莫之與二也。

translations.literal: Though what ritual vessels record and what Odes and Documents praise—the crowning of merit—none stands second to this.
translations.idiomatic: Though ritual vessels record it and Odes and Documents praise it, no crowning of merit stands second to this.

sentences.zh: 遂偃武修文，誕敷德政，八統以馭萬民，九職以刑邦國，思兼三王，以施四事。

translations.literal: Thus he halted arms and cultivated letters, broadly spread virtuous government, used the eight threads to govern the ten thousand people and the nine duties to judge the state, thinking to embrace the three kings and apply the four affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he halted arms and cultivated letters, spread virtuous government, governed the people with the eight threads and judged the state with the nine duties, thinking to embrace the three kings and apply the four affairs.

sentences.zh: 故能信著幽顯，義感殊方。

translations.literal: Therefore trust showed in the hidden and manifest, and righteousness moved the distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore trust showed in the hidden and manifest, and righteousness moved distant lands.

sentences.zh: 自歷世所賓，舟車所暨，靡不謳歌仁德，抃舞來庭。

translations.literal: From ages that honored him, from places boats and chariots reached—none failed to sing of benevolent virtue and leap in dance to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: From ages that honored him to lands boats and chariots reached, none failed to sing of benevolent virtue and dance their way to court.

sentences.zh: 朕每敬惟道勳，永察符運，天之曆數，實在爾躬。

translations.literal: We each time reverently consider the Way’s merit and forever examine the talisman of fortune; Heaven’s allotted span truly rests upon your person.
translations.idiomatic: We each time reverently consider the Way’s merit and examine the talisman of fortune; Heaven’s allotted span truly rests upon you.

sentences.zh: 是以五緯升度，屢示除舊之迹；

translations.literal: Therefore the five cords rose in degree and repeatedly showed traces of removing the old;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the five planets rose in degree and repeatedly showed signs of removing the old;

sentences.zh: 三光協數，必昭布新之祥。

translations.literal: the three luminaries harmonized in number and surely displayed omens of spreading the new.
translations.idiomatic: the three luminaries harmonized in number and surely displayed omens of spreading the new.

sentences.zh: 圖讖禎瑞，皎然斯在。

translations.literal: Charts, prophecies, and auspicious omens plainly stood forth.
translations.idiomatic: Charts, prophecies, and auspicious omens stood forth plainly.

sentences.zh: 加以龍顏英特，天授殊姿，君人之表，煥如日月。

translations.literal: Added to this, the dragon countenance is heroic and outstanding, Heaven bestowed a special posture; the mark of a ruler shines like sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, his dragon countenance is heroic, Heaven bestowed a special posture, and the mark of a ruler shines like sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 傳稱「惟天為大，惟堯則之」。

translations.literal: The tradition says, "Only Heaven is great; only Yao modeled himself on it."
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says, "Only Heaven is great; only Yao modeled himself on it."

sentences.zh: 詩云：「有命自天，命此文王。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "There is a mandate from Heaven; Heaven commanded this King Wen."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "There is a mandate from Heaven; Heaven commanded this King Wen."

sentences.zh: 」夫「或躍在淵」者，終饗九五之位；

translations.literal: " He who "perhaps leaps in the abyss" in the end enjoys the position of the fifth nine;
translations.idiomatic: He who "perhaps leaps in the abyss" in the end enjoys the position of the fifth nine;

sentences.zh: 「勳格天地」者，必膺大寶之業。

translations.literal: he whose "merit grids heaven and earth" must receive the great treasure’s enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: he whose "merit grids heaven and earth" must receive the great treasure’s enterprise.

sentences.zh: 昔土德告沴，傳祚于我有晉；

translations.literal: Formerly when the Earth virtue announced its calamity, the succession passed to Our Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when the Earth virtue announced its calamity, the succession passed to Our Jin;

sentences.zh: 今曆運改卜，永終于茲，亦以金德而傳于宋。

translations.literal: now the calendar and fortune change divination and end forever here—likewise the Metal virtue passes to Song.
translations.idiomatic: now the calendar and fortune change and end here—likewise the Metal virtue passes to Song.

sentences.zh: 仰四代之休義，鑒明昏之定期，詢于羣公，爰逮庶尹，咸曰休哉，罔違朕志。

translations.literal: Looking up to the fine righteousness of the four ages and mirroring the fixed term of brightness and darkness, We inquired of the high lords and reached to the common directors; all said, "Excellent!" None went against Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to the fine righteousness of the four ages and mirroring the fixed term of rise and fall, We inquired of the high lords and common directors; all said, "Excellent!" None went against Our intent.

sentences.zh: 今遣使持節、兼太保、散騎常侍、光祿大夫澹，兼太尉、尚書宣範奉皇帝璽綬，受終之禮，一如唐虞、漢魏故事。

translations.literal: Now envoys holding credentials, jointly Grand Guardian, Palace Attendant Gentlemen of the Regular Companion, Household Grandee Dan, jointly Grand Commandant, Master of Writing Xuanfan, bearing the imperial seal-cord, performed the rites of receiving the end, all according to Tang-Yao and Han-Wei precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys led by Dan, bearing the imperial seal and cord, performed the succession rites as in the Tang-Yao and Han-Wei precedents.

sentences.zh: 王其允答人神，君臨萬國，時膺靈祉，酬于上天之眷命。

translations.literal: King, accord with human beings and spirits, rule the ten thousand states, timely receive spiritual blessing, and requite Heaven’s entrusted mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Accept the mandate of Heaven and men, rule the myriad realms, receive Heaven’s blessing, and answer the charge Heaven has laid upon you.

sentences.zh: 王奉表陳讓，晉帝已遜琅邪王第，表不獲通。

translations.literal: The King submitted a memorial declining; the Jin emperor had already retired to the Prince of Langye’s residence, and the memorial could not be delivered.
translations.idiomatic: The King memorialized to decline, but the Jin emperor had already moved to the Prince of Langye’s residence and the memorial never reached him.

sentences.zh: 於是陳留王虔嗣等二百七十人，及宋臺羣臣，並上表勸進。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Chenliu Qian Si and others, two hundred seventy men, and the host of ministers of the Song Terrace all memorialized urging accession.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince of Chenliu Qian Si and two hundred seventy others, with the ministers of the Song court, all memorialized urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 上猶不許。

translations.literal: Above still did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He still refused.

sentences.zh: 太史令駱達陳天文符瑞數十條，羣臣又固請，王乃從之。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Luo Da presented dozens of items of celestial signs and omens; the host of ministers again firmly requested, and the King then followed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Luo Da cited dozens of heavenly portents; the ministers pressed again, and at last the King assented.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 未能菲躬儉 嚴可均云：「儉下疑奪一字。

translations.literal: Unable to make his person frugal—Yan Kejun says: "Below ‘frugal’ one character may be missing."
translations.idiomatic: Unable to make his person frugal—Yan Kejun notes that a character may be missing after “frugal.”

sentences.zh: 」殿本考證云：「躬下當有節字。

translations.literal: The Palace Edition commentary says: "Below ‘person’ there should be the character for ‘restraint.’"
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Edition commentary proposes that “restraint” should follow “person.”

sentences.zh: 或儉下脫一用字。」

translations.literal: Or one character meaning ‘use’ may have dropped below ‘frugal.’"
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, the word “use” may have been lost after “frugal.”

sentences.zh: 公乃進督 「乃」南史作「仍」。

translations.literal: The Duke then advanced in overall supervision—"then" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "still."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke then advanced in overall supervision—the Southern History reads “still” for “then.”

sentences.zh: 乃速申於當年 「申」各本並譌「由」，據建康實錄、元龜四八六改。

translations.literal: Then swiftly declared it in that year—"declared" in all editions is wrongly written as "from"; corrected according to the Veritable Records of Jiankang and the Yuan Gui 486.
translations.idiomatic: Then swiftly declared it in that year—all editions wrongly read “from” for “declare”; corrected from the Veritable Records of Jiankang and Yuan Gui 486.

sentences.zh: 復加黃鉞 錢大昕廿二史考異云：「加當作假。

translations.literal: Again added the yellow battle-axe—Qian Daxin in Notes on the Twenty-two Histories says: "‘Added’ should read ‘borrowed.’"
translations.idiomatic: Again added the yellow battle-axe—Qian Daxin argues that “added” should read “borrowed.”

sentences.zh: 使持節得殺二千石以下，假黃鉞則可專戮節將矣。」

translations.literal: Holding credentials one may execute those at two thousand piculs and below; borrowing the yellow battle-axe one may exclusively punish commanders bearing credentials."
translations.idiomatic: With credentials one may execute officials of two thousand piculs and below; with a borrowed yellow battle-axe one may punish commanders on one’s own authority."

sentences.zh: 卜世未改 「卜世」各本並作「十世」。

translations.literal: The allotted age of the dynasty was not yet changed—"allotted age" in all editions reads "ten generations."
translations.idiomatic: The allotted age of the dynasty was not yet changed—all editions read “ten generations” for “allotted age.”

sentences.zh: 按自西晉武帝至東晉安帝，已十四世，言十世，無據。

translations.literal: From Western Jin Emperor Wu to Eastern Jin Emperor An there were already fourteen generations; to speak of ten generations has no basis.
translations.idiomatic: From Western Jin Emperor Wu to Eastern Jin Emperor An is already fourteen generations; “ten generations” has no warrant.

sentences.zh: 「十世」當是「卜世」之誤，今改正。

translations.literal: "Ten generations" should be the error for "allotted age"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: “Ten generations” is the error for “allotted age”; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 去秋遣康之送還司馬君者 「君」各本並作「軍」，據晉書譙剛王遜傳玄孫休之附傳、元龜七二五改。

translations.literal: Last autumn sending Kangzhi to escort back the Lord of Sima—"lord" in all editions reads "army"; corrected according to the Jin History biography of Prince Qiao Gang Wang Xun’s great-grandson Xiuzhi and Yuan Gui 725.
translations.idiomatic: Last autumn sending Kangzhi to return the Sima lord—all editions read “army” for “lord”; corrected from the Jin History and Yuan Gui 725.

sentences.zh: 此公之大節 各本並脫「大」字，據南史、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: This was the Duke’s great constancy—all editions omit the character "great"; supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: This was the Duke’s great constancy—all editions drop “great”; restored from the Southern History and Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 一朝掃滌 「滌」各本並作「濟」，據南史、建康實錄改。

translations.literal: Swept clean in one morning—"swept" in all editions reads "crossed"; corrected according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Swept clean in one morning—all editions read “crossed” for “swept”; corrected from the Southern History and Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 今命使持節兼太尉尚書左僕射晉寧縣五等男湛授相國印綬 各本脫「今」字、「兼」字，並據南史、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: Now command envoys holding credentials, jointly Grand Commandant, Master of Writing, Left Vice Director, Duke of fifth rank of Jinning county Zhan to confer the Chancellor of State seal-cord—all editions omit "now" and "jointly"; supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Now command envoys to confer the seal-cord—all editions omit “now” and “jointly”; restored from the Southern History and Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 金虎符第一至第五左 「第五」各本作「第十」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Gold tiger tally first through fifth on the left—"fifth" in all editions reads "tenth"; corrected according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Gold tiger tally first through fifth on the left—all editions read “tenth” for “fifth”; corrected from the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 其以相國總百揆 各本並脫「以」字，據南史、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: Let the Chancellor of State oversee the hundred officials—all editions omit "let"; supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Chancellor of State oversee the hundred officials—all editions omit “let”; restored from the Southern History and Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 上送所假節侍中貂蟬中外都督太傅太尉印綬 各本並脫「貂蟬」二字，據南史、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: Submit upward the borrowed credentials, Palace Attendant sable cicada, Commander of Court and Country, Grand Tutor, Grand Commandant seal-cord—all editions omit the two characters "sable cicada"; supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Submit the borrowed credentials, Palace Attendant insignia, and seals of office—all editions omit “sable cicada”; restored from the Southern History and Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「按宋、齊志皆不見侍中印綬，蓋但給朝服武冠貂蟬而巳。

translations.literal: Sun Miao in Critical Discussion of the History of Song says: "According to the Song and Qi offices, neither shows Palace Attendant seal-cord; probably only court robes, martial cap, and sable cicada were given."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Miao notes that Song and Qi office lists show no Palace Attendant seal-cord—likely only court dress, martial cap, and sable cicada were granted.

sentences.zh: 南史侍中下有貂蟬二字，是。」

translations.literal: The History of the Southern Dynasties has the two characters "sable cicada" below Palace Attendant—this is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern History’s “sable cicada” after Palace Attendant is correct."

sentences.zh: 置宋國侍中黃門侍郎尚書左丞郎隨大使奉迎 「郎」三朝本、北監本、毛本、局本同。

translations.literal: Establish Song state Palace Attendant, Yellow Gate Vice Director, Master of Writing Left Assistant, Gentlemen, following the great envoy in welcoming—"Gentlemen" in the Three Dynasties edition, Northern Directorate edition, Mao edition, and Bureau edition are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Establish Song state Palace Attendant, Yellow Gate Vice Director, Master of Writing Left Assistant, and Gentlemen to follow the envoy in welcoming—the Three Dynasties, Northern Directorate, Mao, and Bureau editions agree on “Gentlemen.”

sentences.zh: 殿本、南史作「相」。

translations.literal: The Palace Edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties read "chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Edition and Southern History read “chancellor.”

sentences.zh: 李慈銘越縵堂日記補云：「當作即隨大使奉迎。」

translations.literal: Li Ciming in Supplement to the Diary of the Yue Mantang says: "It should read ‘then follow the great envoy in welcoming.’"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming proposes the reading “then follow the great envoy in welcoming.”

sentences.zh: 風雲玄感 「玄」各本並作「言」，據局本、文選、建康實錄、元龜二一０改。

translations.literal: Wind and clouds mysteriously moved—"mysterious" in all editions reads "words"; corrected according to the Bureau edition, Wen Xuan, Veritable Records of Jiankang, and Yuan Gui 210.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and clouds mysteriously moved—all editions read “words” for “mysterious”; corrected from the Bureau edition, Wen Xuan, Veritable Records of Jiankang, and Yuan Gui 210.

sentences.zh: 以徐州之海陵北東海北譙北梁豫州之新蔡兗州之北陳留司州之陳郡汝南潁川滎陽十郡增宋國 「北東海」上之「北」字，各本並脫去。

translations.literal: With Xuzhou’s Hailing north, Eastern Sea north, Qiao north, Liang, Yuzhou’s Xincai, Yanzhou’s northern Chenliu, Sizhou’s Chen commandery, Runan, Yingchuan, Xingyang—ten commanderies to enlarge the Song state—the character "north" above "Eastern Sea" is dropped in all editions.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commanderies added to enlarge the Song state—the “north” before Eastern Sea is missing in all editions.

sentences.zh: 據南史、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: Supplemented according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Restored from the Southern History and Veritable Records of Jiankang.
